question: Which state has declared tidal flooding along its coastline as a State-specific disaster?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Kerala.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **Kerala has declared tidal flooding along its coastline a State-specific disaster, enabling affected families to receive financial assistance under the State Disaster Response Fund (SDRF).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kerala is the first state in India to officially recognise tidal flooding as a State-specific disaster. **
 
• Tidal flooding occurs when the Arabian Sea temporarily rises above a set threshold and inundates low-lying coastal areas. 
 
• The declaration allows victims to receive relief similar to other natural disasters under the SDRF. 
 
• Areas prone to frequent tidal floods include regions along Kerala’s coastline such as Vypin and Chellanam. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Tidal Flooding**__

 __
 
• Occurs when sea levels rise temporarily above normal during high tides, especially during full and new moon phases.
 
• Also known as “sunny day flooding” or “nuisance flooding.” 
 
 
 
• **State Disaster Response Fund (SDRF)**__
 __
 
• A fund constituted by the Government of India to provide financial assistance to states for disaster relief and rehabilitation. 
 
 
 
• **State-specific disaster**__
 
 
• A disaster category that a state government can declare under the Disaster Management Act if a natural phenomenon causes significant damage to life and property.
